books.title: 504 Absolutely Essential Words
books.author: Murray Bromberg · Julius Liebb · Arthur Traiger
books.about_en: The classic word list every learner meets first: twelve words a lesson, each with a meaning, a plain definition and sentences that show it working.
books.about_fa: فهرست کلاسیک واژه‌ها؛ در هر درس دوازده واژه، با معنی، تعریف ساده و چند جمله که کاربردش را نشان می‌دهد.

words.def_en: to leave someone or something behind for good, with no plan to come back
examples: They abandoned the car when the road flooded.
She abandoned her plan to study law after one term.

words.def_en: very eager to do something; or sharp, as a mind, an eye or a sense
examples: He is keen to start his new job.
A keen eye will notice the small difference.

words.def_en: unhappy because someone has what you want, or afraid of losing someone you love
examples: He was jealous of his brother's new bike.
She felt jealous when her friend was chosen instead of her.

words.def_en: the skill of saying a difficult thing without upsetting the person who hears it
examples: She told him about the mistake with great tact.
A teacher needs tact as much as knowledge.

words.def_en: a formal promise, often made before a judge, that what you say is true
examples: The witness took an oath before speaking.
He broke his oath and lost their trust.

words.def_en: empty; not occupied by anyone, or not being used
examples: The seat next to me was vacant.
They moved into a vacant office on the second floor.

words.def_en: serious difficulty and suffering, usually over a long time
examples: The family faced years of hardship after the factory closed.
She never forgot the hardships of her first winter there.

words.def_en: brave and polite, especially towards someone in danger or in need of help
examples: A gallant young officer carried the child out of the fire.
His gallant attempt to save the boat was praised by everyone.

words.def_en: facts and numbers collected so that they can be studied
examples: The data show that the new method works.
We collected data from two hundred students.

words.def_en: not used to something, so that it feels strange to you
examples: He was unaccustomed to speaking in public.
Her eyes were unaccustomed to the bright light.

words.def_en: an unmarried man; also the first university degree
examples: My uncle stayed a bachelor until he was forty.
She finished her bachelor's degree last spring.

words.def_en: to reach the standard that a job, a course or a competition asks for
examples: He qualified as a doctor after six years.
Only two runners qualified for the final.

words.def_en: dark, dull and depressing, as a place, the weather or a mood can be
examples: The room looked dismal after the storm.
It was a dismal morning, grey from the first light.

words.def_en: to risk money on the result of a game or an event
examples: He wagered ten dollars on the last race.
She wagered her brother that the train would be late.

words.def_en: serious danger, the kind that can harm or kill
examples: The sailors were in peril when the storm struck.
He set out in the snow, blind to the peril ahead.

words.def_en: to lie back or lean back in a relaxed position
examples: She reclined on the sofa and closed her eyes.
The seat reclines almost flat for sleeping.

words.def_en: to give a loud, high cry, from fear or delight
examples: The children shrieked with delight in the water.
We heard a shriek from the garden and ran out.

words.def_en: seeming evil, dishonest or threatening without saying so plainly
examples: There was something sinister about the empty house.
The letter carried a sinister warning.

words.def_en: to hide something carefully so that it cannot be seen or found
examples: He concealed the key under a loose stone.
She could not conceal her disappointment.

words.def_en: to live in a place, as people or animals do
examples: Few animals inhabit the desert.
The old house is no longer inhabited.

words.def_en: extremely cold; also unfriendly in manner
examples: A frigid wind came off the lake.
She gave him a frigid look and walked on.

words.def_en: unable to feel or move a part of the body, from cold or shock
examples: My fingers were numb with cold.
The injection made his arm go numb.

words.def_en: the body of a dead person or animal
examples: The police found a corpse beside the river.
A corpse lay under a sheet on the ground.

words.def_en: to make someone want something, often something they should not have
examples: The smell of fresh bread tempted me into the shop.
Do not tempt him with offers he cannot refuse.

words.def_en: happening once every year, or calculated over one year
examples: The company holds an annual meeting in June.
Her annual income rose a little last year.

words.def_en: to mix two or more things so that they become one
examples: Blend the flour and butter together.
The tea is blended from three kinds of leaf.

words.def_en: the smallest amount that is possible or allowed
examples: We keep the cost to a minimum.
The minimum for the course is two hours a week.

words.def_en: a natural ability to do something well
examples: She has a talent for explaining difficult ideas.
The choir is full of young talent.

words.def_en: to make someone agree to do something by giving them reasons
examples: He persuaded his brother to lend him the car.
I was persuaded by her argument.

words.def_en: able to be seen, or easy to notice
examples: The mountain is visible from our window.
There was a visible change in his face.

words.def_en: showing the usual qualities of a person, place or thing
examples: It was a typical winter morning, cold and grey.
That answer is typical of him.

words.def_en: to think of a plan, method or tool that did not exist before
examples: They devised a cheap way to filter the water.
She devised a plan to finish the work in a week.

words.def_en: completely necessary, so that something cannot work without it
examples: Water is essential for life.
It is essential to check the figures twice.

words.def_en: sold in large amounts to shops, which then sell it to others
examples: He buys the fruit at wholesale prices.
The wholesale market opens before dawn.

words.def_en: not available in enough quantity for everyone who needs it
examples: Clean water is scarce in the region.
Tickets were scarce, so we bought them early.

words.def_en: costing a lot of money
examples: That restaurant is too expensive for a weeknight.
Repairing the roof was expensive.

words.def_en: having a lot of water in the air, so that the heat feels heavy
examples: The kitchen was hot and humid.
Summer here is humid from morning to night.

words.def_en: to disappear suddenly, often without a sign
examples: The keys vanished from the table.
He vanished into the crowd.

words.def_en: packed closely together, so that air or light hardly gets through
examples: A dense fog covered the road.
The forest here is very dense.

words.def_en: to say what you think will happen before it happens
examples: Nobody can predict the weather a month ahead.
They predicted a heavy harvest this year.

words.def_en: the bad character in a story, or a person who does evil
examples: The villain of the novel is never named.
He played the villain and enjoyed every minute.

words.def_en: the gas that a liquid becomes when it is heated
examples: Vapor rose from the boiling pot.
In cold air the vapor of your breath shows white.

words.def_en: extremely large in size or amount
examples: An enormous tree stood in the garden.
The project cost an enormous amount of money.

words.def_en: an idea or set of ideas offered to explain something
examples: Darwin's theory changed biology.
In theory the plan works, but nobody has tried it.

words.def_en: to use something in a practical way, especially a resource
examples: The farm utilizes every drop of rain water.
We utilized the space under the stairs.

words.def_en: to go down from a higher place to a lower one
examples: The plane began to descend toward the runway.
We descended the stairs in the dark.

words.def_en: to remove something completely, or to take a team out of a contest
examples: The new rules eliminate most paperwork.
They were eliminated in the first round.

words.def_en: to move around a system or a group, as air or news does
examples: Warm air circulates through the room.
The story circulated for a week before anyone denied it.

words.def_en: belonging to the countryside rather than a town
examples: The clinic serves five rural villages.
He grew up in a rural area with no bus service.

words.def_en: the land and buildings of a university or a large school
examples: The library stands in the middle of the campus.
Students live on campus in the first year.

words.def_en: to escape something by doing it in a clever, indirect way
examples: He evaded the question with a joke.
The boat evaded the police and left the harbour.

words.def_en: the larger part of a group, more than half the people
examples: The majority of the class chose the earlier time.
She won by a large majority.

words.def_en: to bring people together, or to put the parts of something together
examples: The whole staff assembled in the hall.
It took an hour to assemble the new shelves.

words.def_en: a habit or custom passed down through the years in a family or people
examples: It is a tradition to eat fish on that night.
The school keeps the tradition alive.

words.def_en: a heavy load of work, worry or cost that a person must carry
examples: The cost became a burden on the family.
He carried the burden of the debt alone.

words.def_en: to travel through a place to find out about it, or to examine an idea
examples: They explored the caves north of the town.
We should explore every option before deciding.

words.def_en: a change made to improve a law, a system or an institution
examples: The tax reform helped small businesses.
He spent his life calling for education reforms.

words.def_en: the subject that a talk, a lesson or a piece of writing is about
examples: The topic of the lesson was food.
We changed the topic before it turned into an argument.

words.def_en: to ask careful questions or look closely into something hidden
examples: The reporter probed the reasons for the delay.
Doctors probed the wound to see how deep it was.

words.def_en: a formal discussion in which people give opposing reasons
examples: The debate about the road lasted three hours.
She spoke well in the class debate.
